newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends on open after test higher fails.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends on open after test higher fails.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended a dull session where it began on Monday after failing a test of its next chart point.
The Kiwi opened 30 basis points higher than its Friday close, at US$0.6939/41, but could not break above 0.6950, ending back at the opening level.
Bankers Trust dealer Philip Lindberg said the failure of the Australian dollar to penetrate US$0.7930 ensured the Kiwi would not crack its next psychological barrier.
On the Trade-Weighted Index, the New Zealand dollar ended at 65.65 from a 65.62 opening.
A holiday in Hong Kong dampened what little enthusiasm there was in the market.

The impending election on October 12 is still not exciting interest and markets have blissfully refused to focus on a poll published on Friday showing support for the governing National Party down three points to 34 percent while the three main opposition parties mustered 57 percent support.
Dealers said they expect further eurokiwi issues to keep the currency underpinned although they did not have wind of specific issues.
